content.title: How Americans Can Get a Driver’s License in Mexico
content.text: To obtain a Mexican driver’s license, you must first have legal residency status, a valid passport, and proof of address in Mexico, a medical check, and a written exam. For short stays, Americans can drive in Mexico with a US driver’s license, but long-term residents need a Mexican license. Driving rules and road culture in Mexico differ from those in the United States, so understanding Mexico’s requirements can help you avoid fines and ensure safe travel, whether you plan to visit Mexico for a short time or stay for the long term. What better way to experience Mexico than by driving through its diverse landscapes, especially if you have access to quality healthcare if needed? From Mexico City to the tranquil countryside, every kilometer traveled is an opportunity to experience the country’s captivating beauty firsthand. Requirements for U.S. Drivers Getting Licensed in Mexico To obtain a driver’s license in Mexico, Americans will need to present their immigration card or proof of legal status in Mexico, a valid passport, and recently issued proof of address. They will also need to pass a basic medical exam, a written test, and a driving test. Short-Term Visitors: Using a U.S. License in Mexico Americans visiting Mexico as tourists and planning to drive can use their current valid driver’s license from the US. However, some car rental companies may require an international driving permit (IDP) along with your original license, so it’s recommended to check with the rental company first. Long-Term U.S. Residents: When Americans Need a Mexican License If you are an American citizen residing or working in Mexico, you will need to obtain a Mexican driver’s license at some point. It is mandatory to obtain a local license within a year of registering a vehicle in your name. Steps to Apply for a Mexican Driver’s License as an American To obtain a driver’s license in Mexico, the same procedures apply whether the applicant has a valid US driver’s license or not. Here’s an overview of the requirements, steps involved, and benefits of using a Mexican driver’s license compared to a US license while in Mexico. Required Documents for Your License Application Prepare the following documents ahead of time for presentation to the Secretaría de Movilidad (Transportation Secretary’s office): Valid immigration document showing legal status in Mexico (FMM, FM2, or FM3) CURP (Unique Population Registry Code) Valid passport Proof of address (recent utility bill within 3 months or bank/phone statement within 2 months) Valid U.S. driver’s license Vision exam certificate (required in some states) Medical Certificate (required in some states) Completed application form Proof of fee payment If the proof of address is not in your name, you can provide a marriage certificate if the person is your spouse. If they are your partner or friend, you must go to the immigration office with the bill in their name to obtain a letter stating that the address is yours. Application & Testing Process Explained After you have gained good familiarity with the law and rules of the road and learned how to properly operate a vehicle, it’s time to: Head to the nearest Secretaría de Movilidad office with the documents mentioned above. Submit your application and documents at the front desk. Pay the application fee in cash (The exact price varies by state and validity period, but can range between USD $33 and $75) Take a simple medical exam, including an eyesight test and a blood test (if you don’t know your blood group). Take the written test, which can be in Spanish or English. The test consists of ten questions, and you can miss a maximum of two questions. If you fail the written test, your paperwork will be held for 15 days, during which you can retest daily. After 15 days, you’ll need to start the process again. After passing the written test, you can proceed to the driving test. One of the skills you’ll be tested on is parallel parking. Once you pass the driving test, return inside, complete the payment process, and provide your photo and fingerprints. Wait for a few minutes for your Mexican driver’s license to be printed. Since the entire process, including the written test, will be conducted in Spanish (English translation is available with some of the steps, but the quality of translation is sometimes the subject of complaint), you’ll need a friend or translator to assist you if you don’t speak Spanish. The validity of Mexican driving licenses ranges from two to five years, depending on the issuing location. It is important to renew driving licenses 30 days before they expire. Driving without a valid license may result in fines. For the most up-to-date and accurate information regarding specific requirements and procedures in different states or regions of Mexico, it is advisable to consult local Mexican government authorities or Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) offices. Why Having a Mexican License Helps U.S. Drivers There are benefits to having a Mexican driver’s license, even for Americans who can temporarily drive in Mexico without one: Simplicity and Convenience: Having a Mexican driver’s license eliminates the need to carry both a US driver’s license and an International Driving Permit (IDP) while in Mexico. Local Identification: A Mexican driver’s license can serve as a valid form of identification within Mexico and may be required for various transactions, such as opening a bank account or dealing with government agencies. Language and Cultural Adaptation: The process of obtaining a Mexican driver’s license involves familiarizing oneself with local driving laws, signage, and regulations, which can help Americans better integrate into the local community and improve their understanding of local customs. Insurance and Discounts: Some insurance providers in Mexico may offer better coverage and discounts to individuals with a Mexican driver’s license. Having a local license may also facilitate the purchase of auto insurance in Mexico. Key Driving Laws & Road Etiquette in Mexico Smooth and safe driving in another country takes more than competent driving skills and good knowledge of the rules of the road. For Americans living in Mexico, it’s essential to familiarize themselves with the road culture in Mexico. Here we provide a succinct summary of the differences between driving in the United States and driving in Mexico. By acquainting themselves with the etiquette of driving in Mexico, American expats can navigate the roads safely and confidently while there. Right of Way: In Mexico, the person on the right typically has the right of way, unlike in the US, where there are specific right-of-way rules. Always exercise caution at intersections and yield to vehicles on your right. Speed Limits: Speed limits in Mexico are usually posted in kilometers per hour (km/h). It’s important to familiarize yourself with the local speed limits, which can vary depending on the type of road and location. Seat Belts: Wearing seat belts is mandatory for all occupants of a vehicle in Mexico. Ensure that all passengers are buckled up, regardless of their seating position. Mobile Phone Usage: It is illegal to use a mobile phone while driving in Mexico unless you have a hands-free device. It is essential to refrain from any distractions and prioritize road safety. Road Conditions and Speed Bumps (Topes) in Mexico Road conditions in Mexico can vary from well-maintained highways to rougher terrain in rural areas. It is advisable to exercise caution and adapt your driving style accordingly. Moreover, topes (speed bumps) are commonly found on Mexican roads, especially in residential areas and small towns. Safe Driving Tips for American Drivers Driving defensively is highly recommended in Mexico. Be prepared for unexpected maneuvers by other drivers and stay vigilant at all times. It is considered courteous to use your turn signals to indicate your intentions and yield to pedestrians. By avoiding aggressive driving behaviors and maintaining a calm and patient attitude on the road, Americans will find driving in Mexico to be not only enjoyable but also conducive to fostering positive interactions with local drivers and residents. FAQs for U.S. Drivers in Mexico Can American tourists drive in Mexico? American tourists can drive in Mexico with their US driver’s license. However, some car rental companies may require an international driving permit (IDP) along with your US driver’s license, so it’s prudent to check with the rental company first. What is the law on seatbelt use in Mexico? In Mexico, wearing a seat belt is mandatory for all occupants of a vehicle, regardless of seating position. Additional requirements apply with regard to toddler and child seats, and these may vary from state to state, so it is best to check them out before hitting the road. Is gas more or less expensive in Mexico than in the US? While gas on average costs the equivalent of USD $0.88 per liter in the US, it costs MXN $24.70 per liter on average in Mexico, which is approximately equal to USD $1.35 per liter as of December 2025. Therefore, gas costs significantly more in Mexico than in the US. Conclusion In this article, we covered the basics of meeting the driver’s license requirements in Mexico for American expats. We also highlighted some important differences between driving in Mexico and in the US. We trust you are now ready to make the right choice for your driving needs.
